options.content:
## Signals to Watch
Four computed ratios derived from collected metrics. Each stat turns **yellow** when it needs attention and **red** when it is out of acceptable range. Green = healthy. Thresholds are conservative starting points — tune them once real production traffic flows through.

panels.title: Review Engagement Ratio
panels.description: Human avg review comments ÷ AI avg review comments. A ratio below 2 means reviewers are engaging with AI PRs almost as lightly as human ones — rubber-stamp risk. Below 1 means AI PRs are getting MORE scrutiny than human PRs, which is unusual and worth investigating.

targets.rawSql: SELECT round( avg(review_comment_count) FILTER (WHERE confidence = 'none')::numeric / NULLIF(avg(review_comment_count) FILTER (WHERE confidence IN ('definite','likely')), 0), 1) FROM pr_metrics

panels.title: AI PR Share %
panels.description: Percentage of all PRs that are AI-authored (definite + likely). Above 50% means AI PRs outnumber human ones — review bandwidth may not keep up. Above 70% is a red flag: the team may be merging AI code faster than it can be properly reviewed.

targets.rawSql: SELECT round( count(*) FILTER (WHERE confidence IN ('definite','likely'))::numeric / NULLIF(count(*), 0) * 100, 1) FROM pr_metrics

panels.title: Escape Rate per AI PR
panels.description: Escaped defects linked to AI-authored PRs divided by total AI PR count. Above 0.1 means roughly 1 in 10 AI PRs is associated with a defect that reached production — watch this trend carefully. Above 0.3 means the review gate is not catching problems consistently.

targets.rawSql: SELECT round( count(DISTINCT e.id)::numeric / NULLIF(count(DISTINCT m.id), 0), 2) FROM pr_metrics m LEFT JOIN escape_records e ON e.source_pr_id = m.pr_id AND e.repo = m.repo WHERE m.confidence IN ('definite','likely')

panels.title: Confirmed Escape Fraction
panels.description: Fraction of all escape records that are commit-linked or manually supplied (vs heuristic time-window). Below 0.6 means most detections are best-effort guesses, not confirmed links — the escape data is less trustworthy. Below 0.4 means the heuristic is dominating and results should be treated as indicative only.

targets.rawSql: SELECT round( count(*) FILTER (WHERE detection_method IN ('manual','commit-linked'))::numeric / NULLIF(count(*), 0), 2) FROM escape_records

options.content:
| Signal | Green | Yellow | Red | What to do |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Review Engagement Ratio** | > 2× | 1–2× | < 1× | If yellow/red: check whether reviewers are actually reading AI-generated diffs, or just approving. Consider requiring a second reviewer for AI PRs. |
| **AI PR Share %** | < 50% | 50–70% | > 70% | If yellow/red: review velocity may not keep up with AI output. Consider enforcing a human-authored PR quota or increasing reviewer capacity. |
| **Escape Rate per AI PR** | < 0.1 | 0.1–0.3 | > 0.3 | If yellow/red: AI-authored changes are reaching production with defects. Tighten the gate policy threshold or require human sign-off on complex PRs. |
| **Confirmed Escape Fraction** | > 0.6 | 0.4–0.6 | < 0.4 | If yellow/red: most escape detections are heuristic guesses. Add `Fixes #<issue>` references in commit messages to improve commit-linkage accuracy. |
